description:
Gives the CLI's `jit search` one executor entry point that returns matches with their issue titles, so the command path stops calling the search module and storage directly.

## Background

The `Commands::Search` arm of `crates/jit/src/main.rs` (or its handler under `crates/jit/src/dispatch/`) builds `jit::search::SearchOptions` and calls `jit::search::search(&jit_dir, ..)` itself, then calls `storage.load_issue(issue_id)` for each result file to print `Issue <id> | <title>` headers. The executor's query family (`QueryOps<'_, S>` via `CommandExecutor::queries()`, in `crates/jit/src/commands/search.rs`) already holds `search_issues` and `search_issues_with_filters`, but nothing covers the ripgrep content search the CLI exposes.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A `QueryOps` method takes the query and search options and returns the content matches, each carrying the title of the issue its file belongs to when it belongs to one.
- [hard] REQ-02: The CLI's `jit search` path calls that method only: it makes no call into `jit::search::search` and no storage call.
- [hard] REQ-03: A harness-level test (`test_search_content_attaches_issue_titles`) shows a match in an issue file carries that issue's title, and `jit search` human and JSON output and its `RipgrepNotInstalled` failure mapping are unchanged with existing suites passing unweakened.

## Notes

- 0f8efc37 later replaces what this entry point computes (one search shared with the server); this work fixes only where the CLI reaches it. 34999aad fixes the ripgrep argv inside `crates/jit/src/search.rs`.
- The JSON `SearchResponse` keeps its shape; whether the title appears in it is not changed here.
- Design rationale: `dev/active/df129d9e-rust-code-quality/plan.md` (D-1, D-11); method inventory: `dev/active/df129d9e-rust-code-quality/investigation.md` area 3.
title: CLI search runs through the executor
